pure-announcement.rationale: A formal engineering specification defining a security framework (RFC 2119 normative language), not a product launch or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: Nearest concepts cover JOSE curve key bindings and agent SDLC change-control tiers; none address key-compromise-resilient signing for software update distribution.

unfalsifiable.rationale: This is the primary formal specification itself, publicly maintained under CNCF with a public reference implementation and conformance test suite — directly checkable, not merely cited.

durability.rationale: The role-separated, threshold-signed key model has been stable since TUF's 2009 origin, is CNCF-graduated, and underpins production systems (PyPI/pip, Uptane automotive OTA, container registries) — it is a mechanism and trade-off, not a version number or price.

actionability.rationale: Gives a concrete adoptable design — offline root key, threshold/quorum trust per role, explicit revocation and re-signing procedure — that directly shapes how someone would build or evaluate a secure updater, not just describe the landscape.

atomicity.rationale: The full spec bundles the key-compromise-resilience model together with several separable concerns — delegation semantics, mirror consistency, specific metadata file formats, and a five-plus-item attack taxonomy (rollback, freeze, fast-forward, mix-and-match, endless-data) — each substantial enough to be its own concept.
